items.title: Punching the Clown
items.summary: Kurt Wagner reinvents his band yet again, this time slimming down to a bare-bones acoustic setup and stripping away the studio artifice. But his storytelling remains as expansive as ever.

items.title: THRASHER
items.summary: With Waylon Jennings’ drawl and a profound sincerity, the Killers frontman sells the blustery, Nashville-via-Utah sound of his gaudy but affecting new country album.

items.title: Reborn
items.summary: The singer tries to fashion himself as a troubled and thirsted-after pop idol on his debut album, but relies too heavily on mall-pop beats and formulaic lyrics to craft a compelling character.

items.title: What Are the Odds
items.summary: On her dance-oriented third LP, the UK singer glides through producer P2J’s tasteful, frictionless blend of two-step garage, UK funky, and house.

items.title: frances chang, “been thinking bout confession”
items.summary: The artfully frayed and lovely third solo record from frances chang tempers the experimental with the musical. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Taking it From the Streets
items.summary: Celebrating the artists who make music on and for the streets. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Weezer (Gold Album)
items.summary: Spurred on by producer Kenneth Blume, Weezer get back in a room together to write rock songs that wallow, reminisce, and, very occasionally, wow.

items.title: The Dark
items.summary: The singer-songwriter returns for a prestige goth reinvention, singing dramatic anthems of self-preservation that feel grander and bolder than anything she’s ever attempted.

items.title: Life in Small Spaces
items.summary: The Brooklyn musician’s synth pop remains almost uncannily retro, but a new emphasis on guitar and sharper-edged songwriting give his latest album a personality of its own.

items.title: All Eyes on Shiest
items.summary: As the Memphis rapper faces life in prison for an alleged attempt to get out of his record contract, the hard-nosed raps on his studio debut are either thrilling or depressing to witness.

items.title: Recto Verso
items.summary: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. This week, we revisit a 2016 album from France that reinvented the decade’s electro-pop as an idyllic Mediterranean dream.

items.title: Gravest Gravy
items.summary: The songs may be familiar to diehards, but on a long-awaited collection of early Alex Chilton recordings they appear in their most primordial form, just sprouting legs and walking on land.

items.title: Hip-Hop Label Fused Arrow Hits The Target, Every Time
items.summary: Helmed by acclaimed producer Steel Tipped Dove, the label is fast becoming an underground rap bedrock. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Essential Releases, August 21, 2026
items.summary: Thrash metal, electronic kosmiche, experimental, and more. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Ok Cowgirl, “Rhinestone Cowgirl”
items.summary: The Brooklyn indie rockers embrace twangy alternative country with confidence and ease. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Gasba Forever: The Next Phase of Algeria’s Millenia-Old Folk Tradition
items.summary: A new compilation explores the idiosyncratic state of contemporary Western Algerian reed flute music. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Herzsprung
items.summary: Like fellow Rhythmic Music Conservatory alum ML Buch, the Danish musician recontextualizes hoary sounds in surprising ways, flipping ’80s AOR and jazz fusion into sleek, mysterious art rock.

items.title: Say a Prayer to the Gods of Getting Going
items.summary: On her fourth record of tender, twangy indie rock, Ella Williams probes the capacity of the open road to cure anything that ails the heart.

items.title: 9 months & 50 hours
items.summary: The British DJ and Mexican alt-pop band livestreamed the production of their new joint mixtape, which highlights a shared interest in freeform music shaped by real-time experience.

items.title: Faith EP
items.summary: The Sacramento rapper’s 16-minute EP is tailor-made for viral engagement, but her outlandish hooks and motivational energy ensure it’s strong enough to stand on its own.

items.title: The Ongoing Transformation of Cabo Verdean Music
items.summary: Past and present, home and afar—a host of elements combine to create dynamic new music. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Learning by Doing: Making Music as Melaina Kol
items.summary: The lo-fi indie rock veteran experiments with spindly string instruments and bubbling vocals on his latest. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Tyondai Braxton, “Splayed Werks”
items.summary: The experimental composer's latest isn't an LP; it's a full-blown anti-album. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Big World
items.summary: Reflecting candidly on aging, forgiveness, and self-improvement, the indie-pop duo returns with a charming new album that takes the world in stride.

items.title: Whatchu Bringing?
items.summary: On a brief new album, the jazz supergroup locks into a relaxed, comfortable groove with communal atmosphere and a hip-hop sensibility.

items.title: Jewish American Prairie Princess
items.summary: Nebraska-raised songwriter Emerson Borakove’s country-fried anti-folk-rock overflows with idiosyncratic humor and tender heart.

items.title: Trapculinary vol.2 (the recipe)
items.summary: The Florida rapper faces off with himself on a hilariously animated new tape, ping-ponging between high and low voices over groovy Florida-via-Michigan beats.

items.title: Open Mike Eagle & Kenny Segal, “DOOMED!”
items.summary: A grim chronicle of post-divorce life on the riveting new record from Open Mike Eagle and Kenny Segal. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.summary: On her latest as L'Rain, Taja Cheek pulverizes walls between genre to arrive at something bracingly new. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.summary: Recorded with Alex Chilton in ’77, the punks' first project was assumed MIA. Then Black Flag's frontman tracked it down. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .
